common_name: Thunder Hens and Chicks (Skrocki Silvery-Rose Sempervivum)

planting.note: Press offsets into lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun; this Ed Skrocki hybrid is grown chiefly for its dramatic seasonal color shift.

directions: Thunder is an Ed Skrocki hybrid whose wide, open rosettes open silvery green brushed with rose and deepen to a smoky lavender through winter cold, sending out hot-pink stolons as the clump spreads. Press offsets into lean, sharp-draining soil in full sun, where the strongest light brings out the richest color; too much shade keeps the rosettes a flat green. It tolerates winters down to -20F without protection, needing only a layer of snow or mulch to ride out the cold, and resents soggy soil far more than frost.

common_name: Bros Hens and Chicks (Heuffelii Deep Red Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; keep drier than common hens and chicks in winter.

directions: Bros is an uncommon Sempervivum heuffelii selection prized for deep wine-red leaves surrounding a bright green center, a color pattern that shifts in intensity with the seasons. Unlike tectorum-type hens and chicks that spread mainly on long stolons, heuffelii rosettes multiply by budding new heads directly at the base, so a single plant slowly becomes a tight, multi-headed mound rather than a loose colony. Give it gritty, sharply drained soil and full sun, and avoid excess winter moisture, since heuffelii hybrids are somewhat less cold-hardy than common hens and chicks.

common_name: Beacon Hill Hens and Chicks (Heuffelii Dusty Purple Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun; keep on the dry side in winter.

directions: Beacon Hill carries the smoky, powdery look typical of many heuffelii hybrids, layering dusty purple over pale green in a soft bicolor wash that shifts with temperature and light. Like other Sempervivum heuffelii selections it clumps by producing new heads at the base of the plant rather than spreading on long stolons, so established plants slowly form a dense mound that can be divided for propagation. Plant in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun and keep it on the drier side in winter, since standing moisture is the main threat to heuffelii types in cold climates.

common_name: Randolph Hens and Chicks (Heuffelii Purple-Tipped Sempervivum)

planting.note: Grow in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; divide clusters every few years.

directions: Randolph's green leaves are tipped in purple to pink, giving each rosette a soft halo of color that becomes more pronounced as the plant matures and the weather cools. Because heuffelii hybrids form new heads at the base instead of sending out long stolons, Randolph builds into a tight cluster of rosettes over a few seasons rather than spreading loosely across the bed. Grow in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun and divide the cluster every few years to keep individual rosettes from crowding each other out.

common_name: Sundancer Hens and Chicks (Heuffelii Fluorescent Green Sempervivum)

planting.note: Grow in full sun in gritty, fast-draining soil to bring out strongest coloring.

directions: Sundancer opens a startling lime green and then lights up in reddish-gold tones through the heat of summer before deepening to burgundy in winter, one of the more dramatic color changes among heuffelii hybrids. Give it full sun and gritty, fast-draining soil, since strong light drives the seasonal shift and the plant stays duller in shade. Like its heuffelii relatives it increases by forming new heads at the base of the clump rather than on stolons, so expect a slowly thickening mound rather than chicks scattered on runners.

common_name: Fire Dragon Hens and Chicks (Calcareum Red-Tipped Mat-Forming Sempervivum)

planting.note: Set offsets into lean, mineral-rich, fast-draining soil in full sun.

directions: Fire Dragon is a calcareum-type sempervivum with blue-green rosettes finished in vivid dark red tips that deepen through the growing season. Set offsets into lean, mineral-rich, fast-draining soil in full sun, where it will slowly knit together into a tight groundcover more than any single showpiece rosette. Sempervivum calcareum, as the name suggests, is naturally found on limestone outcrops in the Alps, so it tolerates lean, alkaline soils that would starve richer-feeding perennials.

common_name: Sunset Hens and Chicks (Tectorum Color-Changing Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; let hens flower and die back naturally.

directions: Sunset is a tectorum selection grown for sheer unpredictability — its many offsets shift through a changing range of colors over the seasons, from green through burgundy to red, rather than settling into one signature look, so a single clump can show several hues at once. Plant in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun and let the hens flower and die back naturally; the surrounding chicks, each coloring somewhat independently, quickly fill the gap. This variability within a single named clone is common in tectorum-derived hybrids and is part of what has made the species the backbone of so much sempervivum breeding.

common_name: Tip Top Hens and Chicks (Calcareum Compact Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant in lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun.

directions: Tip Top is a compact calcareum selection forming small, tightly packed rosettes typical of the smaller end of the genus. Grow in lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun, and resist the urge to feed or water heavily, since rich soil and excess moisture both encourage a loose, leggy growth habit that named sempervivum selections are bred to avoid. As with all hens and chicks, the central rosette flowers only once in its life, on a thick stalk, then dies, so continual offsetting rather than individual rosette longevity sustains the planting for years.

common_name: Coral Red Hens and Chicks (Colorockz Series Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant offsets in full sun in soil amended generously with grit or pumice.

directions: Coral Red is a named selection in the trademarked Colorockz sempervivum series, its rosettes taking on a warm coral-red flush that strengthens under bright, cool-season light. Plant offsets in full sun in soil amended generously with grit or pumice, since standing winter moisture around the crown is the main cause of rot in an otherwise extremely tough plant. Sempervivums have long been planted on rooftops across Europe — the genus name means 'always alive' — on the folk belief that a living roof planting of houseleeks would protect the home from lightning and fire.

common_name: Arctic White Hens and Chicks (Colorockz Series Sempervivum)

planting.note: Grow in full sun and sharply drained, gritty soil to keep coloring crisp.

directions: Arctic White, part of the trademarked Colorockz sempervivum series, carries an unusually pale, frosted look among hens and chicks, its rosettes taking on a silvery-white cast that stands out against the greens and reds typical of the genus. Grow in full sun and sharply drained, gritty soil, where strong light keeps the coloring crisp rather than washing out to plain green. Like other sempervivums it is essentially evergreen, holding its rosette form through winter under snow cover and resuming active growth as soon as the soil warms in spring.

planting.note: Set offsets into lean, fast-draining soil in full sun; keep drier than common hens and chicks in winter.

directions: Mystique is a Sempervivum heuffelii selection whose rosettes develop a moody, shifting color pattern over the growing season, part of the vast pool of named selections maintained by specialty succulent nurseries. Set offsets into lean, fast-draining soil in full sun and space plants with enough room to form a small cluster before they need dividing. Like other heuffelii hybrids it increases by budding new heads at its base rather than spreading on stolons, and it is somewhat less winter-wet-tolerant than common hens and chicks.

planting.note: Plant in gritty, mineral soil in full sun.

directions: Cornelia is a named sempervivum hybrid grown in specialty succulent collections for its well-formed rosette, which blushes deep red under strong sun and cool temperatures. Plant in gritty, mineral soil in full sun, separating offsets from the mother rosette once they have rooted to start new plants elsewhere in the garden. Because sempervivums tolerate being lifted and left bare-root for days without water, named cultivars like Cornelia are commonly shipped and traded between collectors as unrooted offsets rather than potted plants.

common_name: Emerald Spring Hens and Chicks (Globiferum Sempervivum)

planting.note: Grow in full sun in soil that drains quickly after rain.

directions: Emerald Spring opens the growing season in a clean, bright green that gives the cultivar its name, typical of the cooler-season flush many sempervivums show before summer heat and stronger light shift their coloring toward red or purple tones. Grow in full sun in soil that drains quickly after rain, since the plant's tolerance for drought and poor soil is matched by a correspondingly low tolerance for wet feet. Division of rooted offsets in spring or fall is the standard way to propagate it, since most named sempervivum cultivars do not come true from seed.

planting.note: Plant offsets in full sun in sharply drained, gritty soil.

directions: Itchen is a long-established name in the sempervivum collector world, part of the British tradition of houseleek breeding and selection that predates much of the American hybridizing scene. Plant offsets in full sun in sharply drained, gritty soil, and expect the rosette to hold its form through winter with little more than snow or light mulch for protection in cold climates. UK enthusiasts have registered hundreds of cultivar names through specialist societies over the past century, and older British-raised names like Itchen are often harder to trace to a single breeder than more recent trademarked American introductions.

planting.note: Set rooted offsets into lean, fast-draining soil in full sun.

directions: Tesoro is a named sempervivum hybrid held in the expansive collector catalogs maintained by specialty succulent nurseries, grown and multiplied primarily by vegetative division rather than from seed. Set rooted offsets into lean, fast-draining soil in full sun, where consistently bright light keeps the rosette compact and well colored. As with most hens and chicks, the clump persists indefinitely even as individual rosettes periodically flower on a tall stalk and die, since new chicks continually replace the rosettes that are lost.

common_name: Appletini Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Lime-Green Sempervivum)

planting.note: Grow in full sun and lean, gritty, fast-draining soil; divide crowded offsets every couple of years.

directions: Appletini is one of the original releases in the trademarked Chick Charms collection, a line of sempervivum selections bred and marketed for especially saturated, candy-bright coloring — in this case a bright, clean lime green. It has proven influential as a parent, having produced a widely grown sport sold separately as Chick Charms AppleTeaser, selected directly from an Appletini clump showing a color variation worth propagating. Grow it like any hardy sempervivum, in full sun and lean, gritty, fast-draining soil, dividing and resetting crowded offsets every couple of years to keep the colony vigorous.

common_name: Gold Dust Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Speckled Gold Sempervivum)

planting.note: Plant offsets in full sun in sharply drained, gritty soil.

directions: Gold Dust belongs to the trademarked Chick Charms collection bred and marketed for intensely saturated color, its rosettes developing a speckled gold tone that intensifies with strong sun and cooler temperatures. Plant offsets in full sun in sharply drained, gritty soil, since Chick Charms selections are bred from the same tough, drought-tolerant genetics as ordinary hens and chicks despite their flashier coloring. European young-plant growers like Kientzler supply the starts that many North American nurseries finish and sell under the Chick Charms trademark, so the same named cultivar often turns up under slightly different retail branding.

common_name: Grape Galaxy Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Deep Purple Sempervivum)

planting.note: Grow in full sun in gritty, fast-draining soil for the deepest purple color.

directions: Grape Galaxy is a Chick Charms selection bred for deep, saturated purple tones that intensify through the cooler months, consistent with the series' emphasis on dramatic seasonal color over plain green rosettes. Grow in full sun in gritty, fast-draining soil, and expect the richest purple coloring during the cool, bright days of spring and fall rather than in summer heat. Like other named Chick Charms varieties, it is propagated and distributed to retailers as rooted young plants under a registered trademark, even though it is still fundamentally an ordinary, easy-care hardy sempervivum underneath the marketing.

common_name: Pineapple Paradise Hens and Chicks (Chick Charms Gold Sempervivum)

planting.note: Set offsets in full sun into lean, fast-draining soil.

directions: Pineapple Paradise is a Chick Charms selection with warm yellow-gold coloring reminiscent of its namesake fruit, part of a series bred specifically for bold, saturated color rather than subtle variation. Set offsets in full sun into lean, fast-draining soil, since too much shade or rich soil mutes the gold tones back toward plain green. The Chick Charms line is developed by trialing very large numbers of unnamed seedlings and releasing only the most distinctly colored selections for retail sale under trademark.
